instructions:
Controls the Flashback replay mod inside a running Minecraft client through a companion bridge mod.

Basics: time is in ticks (20 ticks = 1 second). Positions are block coordinates. The game must be running with the bridge mod; if a tool says the bridge is unreachable, ask the user to start Minecraft.

Typical workflow: flashback_status -> flashback_list_replays / flashback_open_replay -> scout with flashback_seek, flashback_list_entities, flashback_set_camera and flashback_screenshot (it returns the rendered frame, so look at it) -> write the camera path with flashback_set_keyframes -> check a few ticks along the path with flashback_screenshot -> flashback_export_video and poll flashback_status until it finishes.

Timeline edits are saved automatically by Flashback and can be reverted with flashback_history (or Ctrl+Z in the editor).

tools.name: flashback_status
tools.description: Current state of Minecraft and the Flashback replay editor: state (menu / in_world / replay / exporting), open replay (tick, total_ticks, paused, speed), camera (position, yaw, pitch, roll, fov, dimension), recording state, and export progress. Call this first, and poll it while an export is running.

tools.name: flashback_list_replays
tools.description: List the replay files in the Flashback replay folder with name, length in ticks/seconds, size and date (newest first).

tools.name: flashback_open_replay
tools.description: Open a replay in the Flashback editor. Blocks until it is loaded (can take a while) and returns the status. Any replay already open is closed first, with its timeline saved automatically. If the game is in a world or on a server, it leaves it.

name.description: File name (with or without .zip) or replay display name from flashback_list_replays.

path.description: Alternative to name: absolute path of a replay .zip.

tools.name: flashback_close_replay
tools.description: Exit the open replay and return to the title screen. The timeline is saved automatically.

tools.name: flashback_playback
tools.description: Play or pause the replay and/or set the playback speed. Returns the playback state. With no arguments it just reports it.

paused.description: true to pause, false to play.

speed.description: Manual playback speed multiplier, 1 = real time (0.01 to 100). Speed keyframes override it while they apply.

tools.name: flashback_seek
tools.description: Jump the replay to a tick and wait until the world has caught up. By default keyframes are applied, so the camera moves to where the camera track puts it at that tick. Returns the tick and resulting camera.

seconds.description: Alternative to tick: time in seconds from the start of the replay.

apply_keyframes.description: Apply timeline keyframes (camera, fov, time of day) at the new tick. Default true; pass false to keep the free camera where it is.

tools.name: flashback_set_camera
tools.description: Move the free (spectator) camera. Omitted values keep their current value. Coordinates are the camera entity position (the view point is 1.62 blocks above y; see eye_y in the result). Yaw: 0 = south (+Z), 90 = west (-X), 180 = north (-Z), -90 = east (+X). Pitch: -90 = straight up, 0 = horizon, 90 = straight down. Returns the resulting camera.

look_at.description: Point [x, y, z] to aim at; computes yaw and pitch for you (overrides yaw/pitch).

fov.description: Field of view in degrees (1 to 170). Enables the FOV override in the Visuals settings.

tools.name: flashback_list_entities
tools.description: List entities currently loaded near the camera at the current replay tick, nearest first, with position and rotation. Use it to find players or mobs to frame or follow.

players_only.description: Only players (default true). Pass false for every entity type.

radius.description: Maximum distance from the camera in blocks (default 96).

tools.name: flashback_get_timeline
tools.description: Read the editor timeline of the current scene: scenes, export range, markers, and every track with its keyframes in the same JSON shape that flashback_set_keyframes accepts.

include_keyframes.description: Include keyframe data (default true). Pass false for just the track list.

from_tick.description: Only keyframes at or after this tick.

to_tick.description: Only keyframes at or before this tick.

tools.name: flashback_add_track
tools.description: Add a keyframe track to the current scene. Returns its index. (flashback_set_keyframes with track_type creates a missing track by itself.)

type.description: CAMERA, FOV, SPEED, TIMELAPSE, TIME_OF_DAY, FREEZE, CAMERA_SHAKE, CAMERA_ORBIT or TRACK_ENTITY.

name.description: Optional custom track name shown in the editor.

tools.name: flashback_remove_track
tools.description: Delete a track and all its keyframes (undoable). Indices of later tracks shift down by one.

tools.name: flashback_update_track
tools.description: Enable/disable a track or rename it. A disabled track is ignored during playback and export.

name.description: Custom name; null or empty restores the default name.

tools.name: flashback_set_keyframes

track_type.description: Alternative to track: CAMERA, FOV, SPEED, TIMELAPSE, TIME_OF_DAY, FREEZE, CAMERA_SHAKE, CAMERA_ORBIT, TRACK_ENTITY. Uses the first track of that type.

clear_existing.description: Remove every keyframe already on the track first (default false).

tools.name: flashback_remove_keyframes
tools.description: Remove keyframes from one track (undoable). Select them with ticks, a from_tick/to_tick range, or all=true.

track_type.description: Alternative to track: CAMERA, FOV, SPEED, TIMELAPSE, TIME_OF_DAY, FREEZE, CAMERA_SHAKE, CAMERA_ORBIT, TRACK_ENTITY. Uses the first track of that type.

ticks.description: Exact ticks of the keyframes to remove.

all.description: Remove every keyframe on the track.

tools.name: flashback_history
tools.description: Undo or redo the last timeline edit of the current scene (the editor's own Ctrl+Z / Ctrl+Y history, shared with edits made by hand).

tools.name: flashback_scene
tools.description: Manage editor scenes (each scene has its own tracks and export range): select one, add a new one, or rename one. Returns the scene list.

select.description: For add: switch to the new scene (default true).

tools.name: flashback_set_export_range
tools.description: Set the tick range the current scene exports (the in/out points on the timeline). Without a range, exports cover the span between the first and last keyframe, or the whole replay.

tools.name: flashback_get_visuals
tools.description: Read the Visuals settings of the open replay: HUD elements (showChat, showHotbar, ...), what is rendered (renderBlocks, renderEntities, renderPlayers, renderParticles, renderSky, renderNametags), overrides (fog, fov, roll, time of day, weather, night vision), camera shake, and framing guides / aspect ratio.

tools.name: flashback_set_visuals
tools.description: Change Visuals settings. Pass only the settings to change, using the names and value types returned by flashback_get_visuals, e.g. {"values":{"showHotbar":false,"renderNametags":false,"overrideTimeOfDay":6000}}. overrideTimeOfDay -1 = off. overrideWeatherMode: NONE, CLEAR, OVERCAST, RAINING, SNOWING, THUNDERING. Returns all settings.

tools.name: flashback_screenshot
tools.description: Render one frame of the replay from the current camera to a PNG and return it as an image, so you can see the shot. Optionally seek to a tick first (keyframes are applied, so this previews the camera path at that moment). Takes a couple of seconds. Not available in fullscreen.

seconds.description: Alternative to tick: time in seconds from the start of the replay.

output.description: Absolute path of the PNG to write. Default: <game dir>/flashback/mcp_screenshots/shot_<timestamp>.png

no_gui.description: Hide the in-game HUD. Default: the value last used in the export window.

ssaa.description: Supersample for smoother edges (slower). Default false.

apply_keyframes.description: When seeking: apply timeline keyframes at that tick (default true).

tools.name: flashback_export_video
tools.description: Export the current scene to a video file, driven by the timeline keyframes. Unspecified options use the values last used in Flashback's export window. The range defaults to the scene export range, else the keyframed span, else the whole replay. Minecraft cannot do anything else while exporting: by default this returns as soon as the export has started, then poll flashback_status until state is no longer 'exporting' and check last_export. Not available in fullscreen.

output.description: Absolute output file path (the extension picks the container: mp4, mkv, mov, avi, webm, webp, gif), or a folder for image sequences. Default: Flashback's export folder with its default file name.

overwrite.description: Allow replacing an existing output file (default false).

container.description: MP4, MKV, MOV, AVI, WEBM, WEBP, GIF or PNG_SEQUENCE; also EXR_SEQUENCE on Minecraft 26.1+. An invalid value returns the valid options.

codec.description: H264, H265, AV1, VP9, PRO_RES, QUICK_TIME, ... (must be supported by the container).

encoder.description: Specific FFmpeg encoder for the codec, e.g. h264_nvenc or libx264. An invalid value returns the valid options.

bitrate.description: Bits per second, or shorthand like "20m". 0 = encoder maximum. Default 20m.

transparent.description: Transparent sky; only when renderSky is off in the visuals and the codec supports alpha.

projection.description: PERSPECTIVE (default). On Minecraft 26.1+ also ORTHOGRAPHIC, CUBE_MAP or EQUIRECTANGULAR.

orthographic_zoom.description: Zoom of the ORTHOGRAPHIC projection (Minecraft 26.1+). Default: the value last used in the export window.

depth_map.description: Also export a depth map; needs container EXR_SEQUENCE (Minecraft 26.1+). Default false.

sequence_format.description: File name pattern for image sequences (default %04d).

name.description: Job name shown on the export screen; also the default file name.

wait.description: Block until the export is finished (default false).

wait_seconds.description: With wait=true: give up waiting after this many seconds (default 600). The export itself keeps running.

tools.name: flashback_recording
tools.description: Control Flashback recording while playing in a world or on a server (not while a replay is open): start, finish, pause, unpause or cancel (cancel discards the recording).
